text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that can understand and produce human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns they learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites and articles. Users can improve results through prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions. LLMs are good at tasks like summarizing texts, answering questions and writing drafts. However, they also have limits. They can make mistakes, give outdated information, or produce false facts. For this reason, it is important to check their answers carefully before using them.
